native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In a PCA on the 12 forms of capital analyzed in 100-year time slices, PC1 (31.8% of variance) acts as a general capital-level axis (positive loadings: copper/gold, pottery decoration, hoards, hatchets/swords, daggers, monument size, house size, monument count; negative: pottery form, axes/celts, amber). The Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) is characterized by a steep PC1 decline from a relatively high -0.62 in 3400-3300 BCE (house-size peak Z=+2.05, positive copper/gold) to a phase minimum of -1.85 in 3200-3100 BCE, with a partial rebound to -1.53 in 3100-3000 BCE (net ~-0.9 SD): a phase of elevated capital at the start that is largely lost within two centuries, with the trough coinciding with an axes/celts peak. The Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) is characterized by persistently low, essentially flat PC1 scores (-1.6 to -1.3, net ~+0.2 SD), with no sustained trend except a short-lived spike to -0.75 in 2700-2600 BCE driven by a monument-count outlier (ZMonument=+3.95). Both phases sit at negative PC1 levels well below the Late Neolithic (mean +0.54) and Bronze Age (OBA +2.95, YBA +1.87), i.e., both are low-capital intervals: the MN as a declining phase from a house-size-driven high, the YN as a low, stable phase punctuated by a single monument-count event.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300..500 at 100-year steps; comma decimals parsed; 12 pre-standardized Z-columns, 0 missing). Verified bin anchoring against data/time_series_data.csv (grid value at CE=-X applies to bin X-(X-100) BCE). Ran one SVD-PCA across all 39 slices x 12 variables on the pre-standardized columns (sign fixed so largest |loading| positive); read off PC1 scores for MN bins 3400-3300..3100-3000 and YN bins 2900-2800..2400-2300. Robustness: (a) within-window re-standardized PCAs per window (constant-in-window variables dropped), (b) per-capital-type PCAs using the approved mapping (Symbolic=ZAxtSchwert,ZDolch,Zhausgr; Social=ZCU_AU,Zamber,ZMonument; Cultural=ZKeform,Zkeverz; Economic=ZHort,ZSichel,ZBeil,ZMW). Artifacts: executed script pca_analysis.py, per-bin score table pca_scores_table.csv, loading table pca1_loadings.csv.

sub_hypo.text: The Younger Neolithic has persistently low, essentially flat capital levels, interrupted by a short-lived monument-count-driven spike.
sub_hypo.context: Younger Neolithic, 2900–2300 BCE, evaluated in 100-year bins from 2900–2800 through 2400–2300 BCE using PC1 from the full PCA.

sub_hypo.text: Both the Middle and Younger Neolithic are low-capital intervals compared with the Late Neolithic and Bronze Age, despite differing internal trajectories.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison of Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) with Late Neolithic, OBA, and YBA using the common PC1 axis.
